Recall Newton's second law, which states that the resultant force [MATH: F] acting on a body equals the product of its mass [MATH: m] and acceleration [MATH: a{:}] [MATH: F = ma]

Since air resistance is negligible, the only force acting on the body is its weight due to gravity. The weight [MATH: w] of the body is given by [MATH: F|= w; = mg; = 31g.]

Now, recall that acceleration is the derivative of velocity: [MATH: a=\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t}.] Substituting this into Newton's second law, along with our expression for the resultant force on the container, we get

[MATH: 31g = 31\,\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t}.]

Simplifying and writing in standard form, we get

[MATH: (dv)/(dt)|= g.]

Next, we integrate to solve for [MATH: v(t),] as follows:

[MATH: ∫(dv)/(dt)dt|= g∫dt; v(t)|= gt + C]

Note that [MATH: C] is a constant of integration. We're told that the initial velocity of the container is [MATH: 2.9\,\textrm{m/s}.] So, we apply the initial condition [MATH: v(0) = 2.9,] and solve for [MATH: C{:}]

[MATH: v(0) = g ⋅ 0 + C; 2.9 = 0 + C; C = 2.9]

Therefore, the velocity of the container [MATH: t] seconds after release is

[MATH: v(t) = gt + 2.9.]

Finally, the velocity after [MATH: 7] seconds is

[MATH: v(7) = 9.8\cdot7 + 2.9 = 71.5 \,\textrm{m/s}.]

sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Recall Newton's second law, which states that the resultant force [MATH: F] acting on a body equals the product of its mass [MATH: m] and acceleration [MATH: a{:}] [MATH: F = ma]

In our case, there are two forces acting on the body:

  • The force due to gravity, given by the weight [MATH: w] of the body, which equals [MATH: w|= mg; = 15g.]

  • The force due to drag (air resistance) [MATH: D,] which is proportional to the velocity of the body (and negative since it acts in the negative direction): [MATH: D = -kv,] where [MATH: k>0] is a constant of proportionality. Note that, since the drag, in [MATH: N=\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}^2,] is the product of the constant [MATH: k] and velocity, in [MATH: \text{m/s},] the units of [MATH: k] are [MATH: \dfrac{\text{N}}{\text{m/s}} = \dfrac{\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}^2}{\text{m/s}} = \text{kg/s}.]

Summing the forces, the resultant force acting on the body is [MATH: F = w + D = 15g - kv.]

Also, recall that acceleration is the derivative of velocity: [MATH: a=\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t}.] Substituting this into Newton's second law, along with our expression for the resultant force on the body, we have

[MATH: 15g - kv = 15\,\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t}.]

[MATH: D=-kv = -8v.]

[MATH: F = w + D = 431.2 - 8v.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Consider a body of mass [MATH: m] falling vertically, influenced only by

Content:
- gravity [MATH: g], and
- air resistance (drag) [MATH: D].

Content:
Assume that both [MATH: m] and [MATH: g] are constant, and choose the downward direction as the positive direction.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/06b1b2e20f8bf4bec09fcec8f42a1e7c]

Content:
There are two forces acting on the body:

Content:
- The force due to gravity is the weight, which equals [MATH: mg].
- The drag force is [MATH: D \leq 0], since it acts upward (in the negative direction).

Content:
Hence, the net force on the body is
[MATH: F = mg + D.]

Content:
If drag is negligible, then [MATH: D=0], so the net force becomes
[MATH: F=mg.]

Content:
Applying Newton's second law, [MATH: F=ma], where [MATH: a] is the acceleration of the body, we get
[MATH: F|= mg; ma|= mg; a|= g.]

Content:
Finally, since acceleration is the derivative of velocity, [MATH: a = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t}], we obtain
[MATH: \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t} = g}.]

Item 2 — Tutorial: A Worked Example

Content:
Suppose a supply drone of mass [MATH: 3\,\textrm{kg}] descends vertically. Let [MATH: v(t)] be the drone's velocity, in meters per second, [MATH: t\geq 0] seconds after the descent begins, with downward taken as the positive direction.

Content:
Assuming air resistance is negligible, and the only force acting on the drone is its weight due to gravity [MATH: g,] let's find the differential equation that models the velocity.

Content:
Recall Newton's second law, which states that the resultant force [MATH: F] acting on a body equals the product of its mass [MATH: m] and acceleration [MATH: a{:}]
[MATH: F = ma]

Content:
Since air resistance is negligible, the only force acting on the drone is its weight due to gravity. The weight [MATH: w] of the drone is given by
[MATH: F|= w; = mg; = 3g.]

Content:
Now, recall that acceleration is the derivative of velocity: [MATH: a=\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t}.]
Substituting this into Newton's second law, along with our expression for the resultant force on the drone, we get

Content:
[MATH: 3g = 3\,\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t}]

Content:
Finally, simplifying and writing in standard form, we get

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t} = g.]

What is the velocity of the container after [MATH: 7] seconds? Assume that acceleration due to gravity is [MATH: g = 9.8\,\textrm{m/s}^2.]

Content:

Explanation:
Recall Newton's second law, which states that the resultant force [MATH: F] acting on a body equals the product of its mass [MATH: m] and acceleration [MATH: a{:}]
[MATH: F = ma]

Since air resistance is negligible, the only force acting on the body is its weight due to gravity. The weight [MATH: w] of the body is given by
[MATH: F|= w; = mg; = 31g.]

Now, recall that acceleration is the derivative of velocity: [MATH: a=\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t}.]
Substituting this into Newton's second law, along with our expression for the resultant force on the container, we get

[MATH: 31g = 31\,\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t}.]

Simplifying and writing in standard form, we get

[MATH: (dv)/(dt)|= g.]

Next, we integrate to solve for [MATH: v(t),] as follows:

[MATH: ∫(dv)/(dt)dt|= g∫dt; v(t)|= gt + C]

Note that [MATH: C] is a constant of integration.
We're told that the initial velocity of the container is [MATH: 2.9\,\textrm{m/s}.] So, we apply the initial condition [MATH: v(0) = 2.9,] and solve for [MATH: C{:}]

[MATH: v(0) = g ⋅ 0 + C; 2.9 = 0 + C; C = 2.9]
